title: Eight charged in fraud case - NewsBreak
text: MONROE COUNTY — Eight people have been charged in a credit card fraud case involving jail inmates. The Monroe County Sheriff’s Office took a report from a local bail bondsman in December 2024 who stated he was the victim of credit card fraud. The bondsman stated his company posted bond for five inmates through an online payment processing platform in which fraudulent credit cards were used. The bondsman was subsequently notified by the banks. That crime was found to be part of a larger fraud operated by jail inmates as well as outside accomplices to conspire to defraud, according to a news release from sheriff’s spokesman Adam Linhardt. The suspects, which include five Monroe County residents, identified inmates with low bonds and coordinated to get those inmates bailed out through fraudulent means, Linhardt said. Prior to release, the conspirators added money to the bonding inmate’s commissary account using stolen or fraudulent credit cards. Upon release, the inmates were issued a bank card for the balance of their commissary account, exceeding thousands of dollars. The newly released inmates were then intercepted by other conspirators and instructed to withdraw funds from the accounts, Linhardt said. Those charged and their bonds are: Pretisha Hill, Broward County, $10,000, fraud/swindle and grand larceny;Christopher Alonzo Sweat, Broward County, $385,000, racketeering, money laundering, fraud/impersonation, fraud/swindle, use of a two-way communication device to facilitate a felony, larceny, and grand larceny;Kourtney Breon Wesley, Miami-Dade County, $560,000, racketeering, money laundering, fraud/impersonation, fraud/swindle, use of a two-way communication device to facilitate a felony, larceny, and grand larceny;Darrian Antonio Knowles, Monroe County, $150,000, racketeering, money laundering, fraud/swindle, use of a two-way communication device to facilitate a felony;Eric Cassanova Townes, Monroe County, $100,000, racketeering, money laundering, fraud/impersonation, fraud/swindle, use of a two-way communication device to facilitate a felony, larceny and grand larceny;Tyler Michael Yates, Monroe County, $100,000, racketeering, money laundering, fraud/impersonation, fraud/swindle, use of a two-way communication device to facilitate a felony, larceny and grand larceny;Randy Lamar Barnes, Monroe County, $100,000, racketeering, money laundering, fraud/impersonation, fraud/swindle, use of a two-way communication device to facilitate a felony, larceny and grand larceny; andMichelle Renee Session, Monroe County, $60,000, racketeering, fraud/swindle, use of a two-way communication device to facilitate a felony. Additional arrests are forthcoming, Linhardt said.
